bullets.title: ORCL: Strong Q4 bookings but $70B FY27 capex and $40B capital raise weigh on stock
bullets.body: Oracle reported FQ4 with revenue +21% y/y at $19.18B (beat) and EPS $2.11 (beat $1.96 est), with RPO surging to $638B (+362% YoY) including $75B in customer-prepaid contracts. However, the stock fell 8-10% post-earnings as FY27 net cash capex guidance of ~$70B and plans to raise ~$40B in debt/equity in FY27 (including $20B ATM) spooked investors focused on FCF and margin dilution. Bulls (Citi $330 PT, Mizuho OW, Wolfe raised to $225) see IaaS acceleration at 92%, record bookings, and peak capex visibility; bears note cloud SaaS missed and EPS guide was underwhelming relative to $90B FY27 revenue target.

bullets.title: ADBE: Beats Q2 but CFO departure and organic ARR deceleration trigger multi-firm downgrades
bullets.body: Adobe beat Q2 revenue/EPS and raised FY26 guidance, but FY26 organic ARR guidance was cut ~$480M via freemium strategy shift, while CFO Dan Durn departs to join Marvell effective June 15. Multiple firms downgraded or cut PTs: Wolfe to Peer Perform (PT removed), Evercore to In Line ($225), Stifel to Hold ($200), Freedom Broker to Hold ($250); RBC, Wells Fargo, DA Davidson maintained buys with cuts to $285/$250/$250. Sell-side now 37% Buy; stock at ~7-8x CY27 FCF vs 5Y avg 19-26x.

bullets.title: AMD: Citi double-upgrade to Buy with $575 PT on Meta GPU deal and CPU TAM expansion
bullets.body: Citi upgraded AMD from Neutral to Buy, raising PT to $575 from $460 (~18% upside), citing AMD's Meta MI450 GPU deal (~6GW, 4-year, estimated $15B per GW) and expanded CPU TAM of $137B by 2030 (36% CAGR). Citi sees CY27/28 EPS estimates 12-13% above Street consensus, with AI GPU sales reaching $33B in 2027 and $50.8B in 2028. BofA separately raised the 2030 server CPU TAM to $170B+ citing agentic AI demand.

bullets.title: INTC: BofA double-upgrade to Buy/$135 on hyperscaler interest as NVIDIA alternative; Google TPU packaging deal
bullets.body: BofA double-upgraded Intel to Buy from Underperform with PT raised to $135 from $96 (26% upside), citing INTC's positioning as hyperscaler backup GPU/CPU supplier and leading-edge foundry opportunities. Separately, The Information reported Google is discussing using Samsung for TPU v10 I/O die on 2nm, while multiple sources noted Intel 18A process attracting new customers and Cadence signing multi-year co-optimization deal; INTC +5-9% on the news.

bullets.title: ANET: MS raises PT to $190 on AI front-end networking TAM; CSCO raised to $130
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised ANET PT from $180 to $190 and CSCO from $120 to $130, citing inference-driven front-end network refresh starting with cloud then enterprise. Dell'Oro estimates AI front-end networking spend grows from $1.8B (2025) to $6.3B (2030) at 29% CAGR, with MS upside case of $10B; Arista launched its 7060XE7 1.6T portfolio for Q4 2026/Q1 2027 with Meta, MSFT, ORCL validation. ANET FY28 bull-case EPS ~$7+ per MS.

bullets.title: RH: Q1 beat but Q2 revenue guided below consensus; FY outlook depends on RH Estates launch
bullets.body: RH reported Q1 revenue of $800.3M (beat) and EBITDA of $56.9M (beat $48.8M est), but guided Q2 revenue growth +0.5-2.5% YoY vs FactSet +4.6%. FY26 guidance implies 4.5-8% revenue growth with heavy 2H weighting from RH Estates (~5ppt contribution). UBS maintains Neutral ($45 PT), MS reiterates OW ($240 PT), Citi Neutral ($166 PT raised), KeyBanc Sector Weight. Most analysts flag execution risk on Estates launch as the key uncertainty.

bullets.title: ROKU: Sale talks spark 20% rally; MS reiterates OW on new home screen thesis
bullets.body: Bloomberg reported Roku is in talks to sell itself to at least one U.S. media company, sending shares up ~20% intraday to ~$144. Morgan Stanley reiterates Overweight rating, noting Roku's new home screen as a catalyst. The stock had been under pressure from software sector weakness.

bullets.title: NVDA: Vera CPU launch for China, partnership with Abridge healthcare, OpenAI 10GW Ohio deal
bullets.body: NVDA confirmed it told Chinese customers its new Vera AI data center CPU could ship by August 2026, a key move after GPU export restrictions. Separately, NVDA partnered with Abridge for healthcare AI model training, and is reportedly backing OpenAI's proposed 20-year lease for a 10GW Ohio data center campus. NVDA CEO declined Sen. Warren's invite to testify on AI, and the stock saw outsized influence driving 14% of one S&P 500 day-move.

bullets.title: SMCI: $7B equity raise crashes stock 25-28%; SEC shelf filing follows
bullets.body: Super Micro Computer announced approximately $7B in equity and equity-linked financing to fund AI server orders, causing the stock to plunge 25-28%. The company also filed a mixed securities shelf offering. While order volumes reportedly hit $39B in recent weeks, analysts questioned the dilution and governance risks.

bullets.title: AVGO: $35B XPV platform with Apollo/Blackstone for Anthropic/OpenAI; 20GW target by CY28
bullets.body: Broadcom announced a 20GW AI XPV platform with Apollo and Blackstone (initial $35B tranche) to enable massive ASIC compute deployments for Anthropic (~6GW) and OpenAI (~1.3GW) through CY28, with $128B in Q4 purchase commitments (up from $54B). Revenue per GW estimated at $10-15B. UBS reiterates Buy ($485 PT) on conviction in $130-190B CY28 revenue upside; stock under pressure on Google TPU roadmap uncertainty.

bullets.title: MU/SNDK: Memory supply locked through 2027-28; HBM4 pricing to rise 40% YoY; LTAs accelerating
bullets.body: JPM raised STX PT to $920 and WDC PT to $650 on durable memory pricing cycles; Wolfe raised MU PT to $1,250 citing DRAM ASP +35% q/q in CQ26, HBM pricing +40% YoY in CY27. CSPs are locking 2027 LTA capacity and moving to secure 2028 supply early. SK Hynix plans to triple wafer capacity by 2034; MU earnings call scheduled June 24 with JPM survey showing F3Q26 EPS guide $19.15 vs Bloomberg $19.8.

bullets.title: COHR/LITE: CPO delay narrative overblown per JPM, MS; Lumentum CEO confirms on-track timeline
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis reported CPO scale-up delays to 2030-31 driven by SoIC yield issues, sparking a 15-20% selloff in optical names. JPM, MS, and multiple analysts pushed back as overblown: Lumentum CEO confirmed CPO-supported switch mix >50%, COHR has record bookings through CY27, and LITE CEO stated company is on pace to meet guidance top-end with NPO opportunity 'frankly bigger than CPO.' MS reiterates OW on both with <1x PEG ratios.

bullets.title: DKNG: Prediction markets volumes +34% m/m, no OSB cannibalization; Jefferies turns bullish
bullets.body: DraftKings disclosed May annualized prediction market volumes of $3.1B (+34% m/m), with CEO reiterating no material OSB cannibalization at Jefferies conference (net revenue +24% YoY, sportsbook +30%). Jefferies turned incrementally bullish noting prediction markets access ~50% of previously unreachable US population, doubling TAM without proportional marketing spend. CFTC proposed lenient initial prediction market rules, driving DKNG +15% in two days.

bullets.title: HOOD: Underwriter approval, May AUM +48% YoY, prediction market volumes at ATH
bullets.body: Robinhood received approval to serve as IPO underwriter, expanding beyond selling group member role. May platform assets grew to $377B (+9% m/m, +48% YoY) with net deposits of $5.6B. Director Meyer Malka purchased $20.1M in shares, bringing 7-day total to $55.3M. Needham raised PT to $97; Mizuho raised PT to $115 on prediction market growth ($464M FY26 revenue forecast) with 44.8B contracts modeled in FY26.

bullets.title: SPOT: Citi maintains Buy/$620 on Investor Day; Marketplace ARR/Audiobooks+ ahead
bullets.body: Citi maintained Buy on Spotify with $620 PT after Investor Day, noting small positive estimate adjustments from Marketplace growing 4x (2021-2025) contributing ~50% of Premium gross margin expansion, and Audiobooks+ reaching 1M subs on track for €100M ARR by July 2026. UBS audio survey showed 42% adoption and lowest cancellation intent at 18%, confirming price inelasticity with AI remix/fitness features expanding willingness to pay.

bullets.title: GLW: AWS, NVDA both invest; Amazon signs multibillion-dollar multi-year optical fiber supply deal
bullets.body: Amazon AWS signed a multibillion-dollar, multiyear optical fiber supply agreement with Corning for U.S. data center infrastructure, expected to create 1,000 jobs. NVDA also invested in GLW in May. GLW was down 10.7% for a week earlier in the period but analyst notes highlight the company's growing strategic importance to AI infrastructure buildout.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: DoJ approves Paramount-Skydance deal without divestitures; Australian regulators clear
bullets.body: The Department of Justice approved the Paramount Skydance acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery without requiring divestitures or behavioral remedies, though California AG Rob Bonta could still sue. Australian regulators also approved the Paramount/WBD combination. Foxtel separately emerged as a potential NRL rights bidder, with Paramount/Network Ten named as a sublicensee candidate.

bullets.title: TTD: Publicis-Trade Desk dispute resolved; stock at 52-week lows with ongoing headwinds
bullets.body: Publicis and The Trade Desk resolved their dispute over hidden ad tech fees, with both companies issuing a joint statement on 'moving forward.' However, The Trade Desk remains at 52-week lows (-74.3% YTD), with TTD handles at 52-week lows per StreetAccount. Walmart expanding DSP partnerships, complicating TTD's positioning narrative. Omnicom commenced a full third-party audit of its TTD agreement in March.

bullets.title: NBIS/CRWV/ALAB: Nasdaq-100 additions effective June 22 close drive premarket surges
bullets.body: Nasdaq-100 quarterly rebalance effective June 22 adds Nebius Group (NBIS), CoreWeave (CRWV), and Astera Labs (ALAB) while removing Charter Communications (CHTR). CRWV, NBIS, ALAB each rallied 4-5% in premarket on the announcement. Citi upgraded NBIS to Buy with $287 PT on full-stack AI platform expansion; CRWV gained further on Citi's data center tour showing 97%+ GPU utilization and improved pricing outlook for Vera Rubin generation.

bullets.title: ACN: Wells Fargo OW, upcoming F3Q earnings June 18; positioned as AI transformation proxy
bullets.body: Wells Fargo reiterates ACN at Overweight with investor call scheduled June 18 to recap F3Q earnings. UBS Best Ideas list includes ACN as top pick leveraging AI-led services demand. JPM IT services roundtable flagged ACN organic growth at risk in FY27 creating an overhang, with bears citing AI-driven margin risk and AI disruption—but bulls see ACN bridging AI pilot-to-production gap with strong bookings.
